obligations.note: In `LedgerService.amend_memo` (service.py), the change replaces `self._audit(actor, "amend_memo", ...)` with an application log line. Amending a payment memo is state-changing (it persists via `payments.amend_memo`), and it now records no audit event with actor, action, target and time.
The new `_log.info` call site matches the LOG-1 pattern. It logs only `payment_id`, which is not an NPI field. The sampled logging control test passes.
Ticket CHG-24556 is standard and approved by change manager grace.kim on 2026-10-17, before review. Its components [payments.service] cover the only touched file, service.py.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa, a change_approver for payments. She is a different person from the author, Sofia Santos.
The approval names the head commit c4ac2735, and there are no later commits.

run.json names the head commit on ci-runner-04, started 2026-10-19. The only JUnit report, however, is timestamped 2026-10-23, after the 2026-10-21 review time, and was produced on hostname dev-laptop-7.local. It is therefore not valid evidence from the change's own CI run.
The only touched file, service.py, maps to payments.service, which is not security_sensitive. No security review is required.
No protected path (controls/, control tests, ci/) is modified. No control_owner approval is required.
No exception is claimed, and none in the register covers AUD-1 for payments.service. The AUD-1 deviation is therefore unexcused.
The ledger entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and mortgage files. None of these is changed, so no accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The change removes the audit event for payment memo amendments and replaces it with an application log line. This violates AUD-1: every state-changing operation must be audited, and no exception covers the gap. Separately, the JUnit report is dated after the review time and came from a personal workstation, so it does not validly evidence the CI run on the head commit. The ticket, independent approval and approval-on-head are in order, but the AUD-1 violation requires rejection.
